title: EU Deforestation Regulation applies to large and medium operators
summary: From 30 December 2026, companies placing cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya or wood products on the EU market must file a due-diligence statement proving the goods are deforestation-free and traceable to the plot of land.
what_to_do: List every imported product under the seven EUDR commodities and map it to its supplier.
Request plot-level geolocation and origin evidence from each supplier; set an internal cut-off six weeks before the deadline.
Decide who files the due-diligence statement in your chain and record the reference numbers.
Plan for border holds on shipments that lack a statement.

title: EU Deforestation Regulation applies to micro and small operators
summary: Micro and small enterprises get an extended start date of 30 June 2027 for EUDR obligations, subject to conditions in the regulation.
what_to_do: Confirm whether your company qualifies as micro or small under the EU definition.
Check whether your larger customers will require EUDR evidence from you earlier than the legal date.

title: CBAM certificate sales open
summary: From 1 February 2027 importers of CBAM goods (iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen) into the EU can buy the carbon certificates they must surrender for 2026 imports.
what_to_do: Estimate the embedded emissions and certificate cost for each CBAM product you import.
Budget the certificate purchase in the 2027 plan and decide whether to pass the cost through.
Ask non-EU suppliers for verified emissions data now; default values cost more.

title: First annual CBAM declaration and certificate surrender due
summary: The first annual CBAM declaration, covering 2026 imports, and the surrender of certificates are due by 30 September 2027. Quarterly reports are replaced by the annual declaration.
what_to_do: Keep the 2026 import ledger for CBAM goods reconciled by HS code and supplier.
Hold certificates covering at least 80% of imported CBAM goods at all times from 2027.

title: Nationwide unrest in France over schools, austerity and living costs
summary: Student protests that began in late September 2026 became nationwide cost-of-living unrest; on 17 October about 550,000 marched and roughly 2,400 people were arrested in one day, with town halls, shops and transport hit in Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Lille, Bordeaux and Limoges.
what_to_do: Add 2-5 days of buffer to inbound and outbound lanes through French ports and hubs on announced protest days.
Issue travel and site-safety guidance for French sites; confirm remote-work options.
Check French suppliers' continuity plans and watch for public-sector strike days that close customs.

title: Five French unions call a national strike
summary: Five labour unions in France have called a national strike for 5 November 2026 demanding higher wages and more funding for public services, and invited pensioners and students to join.
what_to_do: Move time-critical French shipments off 5 November; expect reduced customs and rail capacity.
Warn French sites and staff; plan shift cover.

title: Moody's scheduled review of France's sovereign rating
summary: Moody's reviews France on 23 October 2026 while the country's rating sits at Aa3 with a negative outlook and its 10-year borrowing premium over Germany is near euro-crisis highs. A downgrade would raise French borrowing and financing costs.
what_to_do: Review euro-denominated financing and hedges tied to French counterparties.
Watch the French-German bond spread; above 160 basis points signals escalation.

title: French presidential election, first round
summary: France votes on 18 April 2027, with a run-off on 2 May. The National Rally candidate leads polls near 35% and pledges to cut Ukraine aid and France's EU budget contribution, which would change EU trade, budget and climate policy.
what_to_do: Scenario-plan for a change in French and EU policy direction after May 2027.
Avoid locking long-dated French contracts without policy-change clauses.

title: US-Israel war on Iran keeps fuel and freight costs elevated
summary: Since strikes on Iran began on 27 February 2026, diesel in France has stayed above 2 euros a litre and reached a record 2.41; renewed fighting in Yemen and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure have intensified the spike. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea carries war risk.
what_to_do: Re-price lanes through Hormuz, the Red Sea and Suez with war-risk surcharges and longer transit.
Add fuel-surcharge clauses to carrier and customer contracts.
Identify parts with petrochemical inputs and hold extra cover stock.

title: Cost-of-living riots in Milan, Turin and Bologna
summary: Two days of rioting and looting around Milan's Duomo on 17-18 October 2026 brought more than 200 arrests; clashes also hit Turin and Bologna. Prime Minister Meloni called a security meeting. Italy holds a parliamentary election in 2027.
what_to_do: Avoid routing through central Milan on protest days; brief staff at Italian sites.
Watch for strike calls by Italian unions in the coming weeks.

title: Cost-of-living clashes in Brussels and Liege
summary: Police clashed with demonstrators in Brussels and Liege during cost-of-living protests on 17 October 2026; Liege had earlier banned gatherings of more than three people for a period after school protests.
what_to_do: Expect intermittent disruption around Brussels and Liege; keep Antwerp port moves flexible.

title: Spanish strike over housing and wages ahead of snap election
summary: Demonstrators in Spain are expected to strike in November 2026 over housing and wages, two weeks before a snap general election. Exact date not yet confirmed.
what_to_do: Confirm the strike date with Spanish carriers and sites once announced.
